newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus' former leader told to pay $200 penalty.
newsitem.headline: Belarus' former leader told to pay $200 penalty.

text.p: A Belarusian court ordered the speaker of the dissolved parliament on Tuesday to pay a fine worth $200 for taking part in an anti-presidential rally two months ago.
A district court in the capital Minsk found Semyon Sharetsky guilty of violating a presidential decree on rallies and demonstrations and imposed the fine of four average salaries.
Sharetsky took part in the rally on March 15 against the policies of the hardline president Alexander Lukashenko. Authorities have branded the rally, attended by thousands of people, as illegal.
Earlier this year court fined another former parliamentary speaker, Mechislav Grib, for violating the same decree, under which rallies should be authorised by local administrations.
Last November Lukashenko won a controversial referendum, which gave him a sweeping powers which he used to dismiss the old parliament and install a new one.

Lukashenko and Russian President Boris Yeltsin are due to sign later this month an accord putting into force a union treaty, which, Belarus opposition say, could ruin the country's independence, won in 1991.
Lukashenko says a merger with Russia meets the will of the vast majority of the people.
